 ******************************************************************************)

native component FlatString

import String.{maxLeafSize, concatAndBalanceIfNecessary, CatString, spaces}
import Stream.{...}

export FlatString


private language="java"
private package="com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim"

lineSeparator: String = LineSeparator()

private natLineSeparator(): String = builtinPrimitive(
            "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Writer$LineSeparator")

private LineSeparator(): String =do
    ignore(FlatString); (* This initializes the constructor for FlatString
                   before its type is used (in the next line). *)
    natLineSeparator()
  end

object FlatString extends { String, DelegatedIndexed⟦Char, ZZ32⟧ }
    getter size() : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Size")
    getter asExprString() : String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$ToString")
    getter asFlatString(): String = self
    getter asString(): String = self
    getter asDebugString(): String = asDebugStringIndented(0)
    getter depth():ZZ32 = 0

    (* With the help of trait DelegatedIndex, this defines our generate method *)
    getter generator() : Generator⟦Char⟧ =
        self.indices.map⟦Char⟧(fn (i:ZZ32):Char ⇒ self.get(i))

    getter isBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isAlmostBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isExtremelyUnbalanced():Boolean = false

    opr |self| : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Size")

    uncheckedSubstring(r1: Range⟦ZZ32⟧) : String = do
    (* We could build a subString node here, but not until everything is working,
        because that will introduce
       SubString objects into code that may still expect FlatStrings.
       As written, this method always answers a FlatString.
       In any case, the FlatString object supports substring without copying*)
        assert((r1 ∩ self.bounds).isEmpty, r1.isEmpty,
                    "Empty substring of non-empty string")
        if r1.isEmpty then ""
        else self.javaSubstr(r1.left.get, r1.right.get + 1)    (* Java substr's endIndex is one past the last character *)
        end
    end

    opr =(self, other: FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Eq")
    opr <(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) < 0
    opr <=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≤ 0
    opr >(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) > 0
    opr >=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≥ 0
    opr CMP(self, other: FlatString): TotalComparison =  self.cmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CMP(self, other:String):TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CMP self)
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:FlatString): TotalComparison =
      self.cicmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:String): TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP self)

    (** get skips bounds checking. **)
    get(i:ZZ32): Char =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Index")
    cmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Cmp")
    cicmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$CICmp")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32,hi:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Substr")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32): String = javaSubstr(lo, self.size)
    javaIndexOf(c:Char): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$IndexOf")
    flatConcat(self, b:FlatString):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Concat")
    flatConcat(self, b:Char):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Concat")
    javaRegExpMatches(m:FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$javaRegExpMatches")
    javaRegExpSplit(m:FlatString, i:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$javaRegExpSplit")

    indexOf(c:Char): Maybe⟦ZZ32⟧ = do
        i = javaIndexOf(c)
        if i = -1 then Nothing⟦ZZ32⟧ else Just⟦ZZ32⟧(i) end
      end

    verify():() = do
        assert(self.depth, 0, self)
    end

    asDebugStringIndented(indent: ZZ32): String =
        spaces(indent) || "J" |self| "/" self.depth ":" self

    opr ∈(c:Char, self): Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ≠ -1

    rangeContains(r: Range⟦ZZ32⟧, c: Char):Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ∈ self.bounds[r]

    (** The operator %||% with at least one String argument converts to string and
        concatenates **)
    opr ||(self, b:FlatString): String = do
        if b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
             (* Since both self and b have depth 0, balancing can't be necessary *)
            CatString(self, b)
        else
            flatConcat(self, b)
        end
      end

    opr ||(self, b:String):String = do
        if self.isEmpty then b
        elif b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
            concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b)
        else
            typecase b.asFlatString of

content.content:
# The report and the record

## What every report holds

Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.

A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.

A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.

Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:

- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.

## At a point to report

- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
- Then finish the work.
- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.

## Timings and citations

- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.

## POSITIONS and FACTS

POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them.

A FACTS entry is the fact, its source and its test in a few lines, under a bold title. It points to the report that holds the detail. Cite it by its bold title, or by its opening words if it has no title.

## The gap ledger

The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.

- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.

Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:

    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh

- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.

A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.

Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:

    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE

## Writing to the record

- Add a fact to FACTS in the commit that establishes it, as a new entry in the section of its topic. Its source and its test can be the code at file:line, a gated test, or a command and its output. If your brief does not let you write FACTS, put the entry in your report as finished prose.
- Rewrite a wrong line of FACTS in place.
- POSITIONS holds the curator's decisions, in the curator's words, written once. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.

Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.

    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

To add a row:

1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

To change a row:

- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N.
- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it.

## The repository's history

- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.
- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's. After the tag `sealed-tree`, commit `75cca6683`, the revival began to fix the team's code, test first. Before it, the revival changed mainly the build and the toolchain.
- `git diff a874948ac -- FILE` shows what the revival changed in a file, and `git diff 75cca6683 -- FILE` what it changed after the tag.
- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a `git log` of a directory stops at a cut and misses the team's earlier commits. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.
------
# The Claude Code session: the Bash tool, long commands, waits and stops

**prompt cache**
: API's copy of a conversation's context. It lives five minutes for an agent and one hour for the main session. Each request to the API within that time reads the cache and renews it. The first request after a longer wait writes the whole context again: late in a long task, hundreds of thousands of tokens.

**interrupt**
: Stop of the session's turn, by the stop button. It kills every agent that runs in the background at that moment, of the Agent tool or of a Workflow.

**stop of the process**
: End of the session's Claude Code process. It kills every agent. It keeps the conversation, the transcripts and the disk: worktrees, uncommitted edits and logs. A command started with `nohup` (below) survives a stop, but not a restart of the machine.

**automatic permission check**
: Check that approves each tool call in auto mode. It can refuse a call, also a call that the curator approved in chat.

## The Bash tool and waits

The Bash tool stops a call at 120 s, unless the call passes a longer `timeout`, at most 600 s. It kills the command, or moves it to the background. It also refuses a command that starts with `sleep N` and goes on to another command, such as `sleep 60; tail build.log`. Wait with `wait_for` instead (below).

- In an agent, keep every wait under 270 s.
- In the main session, keep every wait under an hour. The main session can also watch a run with the `Monitor` tool.

## Long commands

If a command can take more than a minute or two, start it detached with `nohup`, after the setup lines, whose exports it inherits. Write the command and the log in the line itself:

    nohup bash -c '( ant compileAll ) > tmp/build.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> tmp/build.txt' >/dev/null 2>&1 &

The log gets the output, then a last line `EXIT=<status>`. The automatic permission check refuses a shell function that passes the command to `bash -c` in a variable, because it cannot read the command.

The shell function `wait_for` waits for the `EXIT=` line, for 270 s at most. If the line is there, it prints the log's verdict lines and returns 0: ant's `BUILD` and `Total time:`, JUnit's `OK (`, `FAILURES!!!` and `Tests run:`, and `EXIT=`. If not, it returns 1.

Run `wait_for` until it returns 0, each time in a new Bash call. Give that call a `timeout` above 270 s, such as 300000 ms. Define the function in each call that uses it. Grep the log for the lines that you need.

    wait_for () {    # wait_for <logfile> [max seconds, at most 270]; call again until it returns 0
        local n=0 max=${2:-270}
        case "$max" in ''|*[!0-9]*) max=270 ;; esac ; [ "$max" -gt 270 ] && max=270
        while ! grep -q '^EXIT=' "$1" 2>/dev/null ; do
            sleep 5 ; n=$((n+5))
            [ "$n" -ge "$max" ] && { echo "still running after ${n}s" ; return 1 ; }
        done
        grep -n '^BUILD \|^Total time:\|^OK (\|^FAILURES!!!\|^Tests run:\|^EXIT=' "$1"
    }

## Stopping processes

Stop only the processes that run under your tree's path. To find a process's path, read `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd`, or the paths in its arguments.

Kill by process id, with `kill <pid>`. A pattern, as in `pkill -f`, also matches other agents' copies of the same scripts, and your own call's shell, which it then kills.

## After an interrupt or a stop of the process

If your work starts again after an interrupt or a stop of the process:

1. Read what is on disk first: `git log` and `git status` in your tree, and your logs.
2. If a step's log has ended and the tree has not changed since, the step is done. A log has ended if it has its `EXIT=` line, or its verdict or table is complete.
3. If a log has no `EXIT=` line yet, its command may still run. Look for its process under your tree's path. If it runs, wait for it with `wait_for`.
4. Continue at the first step whose log is missing, cut off or failed.

## When the automatic permission check refuses a call

- Do not try for the same result with another tool, by another route or in a later turn.
- Report the refusal and what was not done because of it. The way through is the curator's: manual approval for the session, or an allow rule for the command (`/permissions`).

1	<!-- A design, written 2026-10-13 at the curator's request before the FACTS and POSITIONS consolidation, for how the record is stored and written: six ways compared, the gap ledger's own first, and the one recommended (each entry one line under a permanent number, the history a dated provenance line per change with the earlier text the tool copies, one write call in a new `record.py` beside `ledger.py` that lands both, number queries in `facts-extract.sh` that return an entry with its linked entries and its history, the checks that replace `check-verbatim.py`, the numbering and the carry-over of the history files and of every citation by title, and its cost), with what not to build and the decisions left to him. -->
2	
3	# The record's store and its tool: a design
4	
5	The curator's question, 2026-10-13 (10:30, 15:32 and 15:51 UTC, dictated): before the consolidation of `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md`, settle how the record is stored and written, so that the workers who consolidate it in chunks and the coordinator after them use one tool. One call writes an entry and its provenance, so nothing is written twice. A lookup surfaces an entry with the entries linked to it, "like a second level cache" behind the compressed record in context. The model's habit of a dated project memory is channelled into the history. Nothing is over-engineered.

65	1. `record.py add F|P --section TITLE FILE [provenance]` gives the entry the highest number ever used in its file plus one, puts it at the end of the section, and appends an `added` block.
66	2. `record.py set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] [provenance]` rewrites entry N in place (FILE holds the whole new line, with or without its number), or moves it, appends a `rewritten` or `moved` block with the earlier line, and refreshes the quoted title words of every pointer to N in both files.

20	## 2. His comments, answered
21	
22	**16:46, on `trace`: does this replace the fact shell script; the workers' skill; backwards compatibility; one line.**
23	
24	- No. `facts-extract.sh` stays the one reader. `record.py` is the one writer, as `ledger.py` is for the ledger. The design's new queries are queries of `facts-extract.sh`, and section 3 cuts `trace:` down to `history:F-87`.
25	- The writer is the coordinator's and the gather's tool. In a batch nothing changes for a worker: it writes the entry as prose in `record.md`, and the gather folds it in, now through `record.py apply` (`climb-batch-workflow.md:97-99`, `:160`). A lone worker whose brief lets it write FACTS runs `record.py add` instead of a hand edit (`records.md:73`). The `fortress-repo` skill's `records.md` changes in about six lines: cite an entry by its number, as a row is cited (`records.md:37` says by its bold title today); the queries `F-87`, `F-87+` and `history:F-87`; and the write call for a worker allowed to write. The skill writer makes that change tonight at step 5; until then `record.py --help` carries it.
26	- Backwards compatibility: the only change a reader sees is `F-87 ` after `- `. Title queries, `section:` and `positions:TITLE` work unchanged once `title_of` skips the number. A citation by title in a dated note resolves as now while the title holds, and through the former-titles line of the history (3.2 below) after a retitle. `fill.py` gets its one-line change. The dated `positions:DATE` fallback into the history stops finding anything after the rebuild; the dated notes that use it are history themselves, and `git show` answers them.
27	- One line: the record is already one line per entry, in both files, and the tool makes it a rule: `add` and `set` refuse a line break. The number stands at the line's start, so `grep F-87 FACTS.md` returns the whole entry, and `grep -c '^- F-' FACTS.md` counts the record. The history keeps the same property: each earlier text is one line, `- F-87 **...**`, so `grep '^- F-87 '` across both files lists every text the entry has had.

Three places where it leaves the ledger's way are brought back: the ledger cites a row by number alone ("duplicate of row M"), has no frozen part with a hash, and prints a row with `show` and its history by number, not a trace through other files. Section 3 does the same.
30	
31	**16:58, on pointers: sections, a flat file, no tags.** The sections stay as they are: FACTS's nine `##` sections and POSITIONS's `##` sections with `###` subsections. An entry's group is the heading it stands under, and that is the whole structure: no tags, no typed links, no stored index. A pointer is a number inside a sentence, and the sentence says what the link means. The consolidation moves a few entries between sections (the outline's 3.2.4 and 3.2.5); `set --section` does that and the tool records the move.
32	
33	**17:01, on the frozen history: rebuild it now.** His comment wins over the design's "frozen byte for byte", on two grounds. It is his word, later than the position on record that the history holds "every earlier text" (`POSITIONS.md:130`), and that sentence of the position is rewritten tonight to say what the history now holds; this is decision 1 of section 5. And nothing live reads the old texts: no skill, no live document and no query but the dated `positions:` fallback.
34	
35	- After the rebuild the history holds, under each number: one `numbered` block from the numbering script, naming the entry's line at the base and the titles it had before (from the old history's texts that match the entry by title: 487 exact and 92 opening matches of FACTS's 959 texts, 63 of POSITIONS's 328); then one block per change from the consolidation on, with its provenance line and the line it replaced. 36	- What leaves the files: the 959 and 328 old texts, 2.5M bytes, in their dated sections. Of them, 334 and 251 match no current title and were never linked to an entry. Nothing leaves git: the parent of the numbering commit holds both files, and the new header names that commit, so `git show HASH:explorations/coordinator/FACTS-history.md` prints them. The scouts read the old texts from there tonight.
37	- The 46 "similar" matches the design leaves for the builder to confirm are not linked: that is judgement, not a script's work, and a missed match costs one citation its fallback.
38	- What keeps the dated notes' title citations working: the former-titles line, written once by the numbering script (about 580 titles, 70K bytes), and from then on the earlier text of each block, which holds the title at the time. 39	
40	**17:02, on the history block: "sounds like YAML".** It is a record with fields: when, what kind, from where, which commit, who, why. No YAML: a YAML block needs a parser the tools do not use, breaks the one-line grep, and is not the ledger's form. 43	
44	- The writer never names a kind. The tool derives it: a new number is `added`; the section changed is `moved`; the number gone is `removed`, or `merged into F-n` when `merge` was run; anything else is `rewritten`. One correction: the small passes also retitle and merge. Today's one consolidation of FACTS retitled 56 of 209 entries and merged 10 (the "titles changed" tables of `facts-slice-1.md` to `-7.md`), so the tool keeps the former titles itself rather than leaving that to a writer.

The earlier line costs the writer nothing, since the tool copies it. What the writer must give is `--from` or `--note`, the one thing git cannot give per entry. So the history is worth keeping at exactly that price and no more.

55	## 3. The design as it should be built
56	
57	For the builder's brief. Each item ends with its status against the design: as designed, changed, or new.
58	
59	**The entry.**
60	
61	- One line: `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in `FACTS.md`, `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in `POSITIONS.md`. A number is never reused or changed. The title and the text are rewritten freely. (as designed)
62	- The tool refuses an entry with a line break. (new)
63	- A pointer is the target's number in the sentence that needs it: `It builds P-48.` Words beside it are the writer's and are not checked. The tool checks only that the number resolves to a live entry. No refresh of other entries' lines on a retitle. (changed: 3.1.2 and decision 4)

70	- A block is the ledger's: `### F-87`, a blank line, one provenance line, a blank line, the earlier line verbatim. The provenance line, in this order: the UTC time from the clock, the kind, `from` each report section, `commit` the hash, `by` who, then the note after a colon. The `numbered` block has no earlier line; its note gives the line at the base and the former titles, each in quotes. (as designed in form; the `numbered` block's content changed)
71	- The kinds are derived by the tool: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved`, `merged into F-n`, `removed`, `numbered`. No `title was`. (changed: 3.2.3)
72	- The block keeps the earlier line. (as designed, decision 2)
73	- A POSITIONS change's `--note` holds his words with their UTC time where they are the reason. (as designed)
74	
75	**The write.** `record.py` beside `ledger.py`, importing its lock, its one-step write and its word matching. Its commands:
76	
77	- `add F|P --section TITLE FILE PROVENANCE`: the highest number ever used plus one, at the end of the section. (as designed)
78	- `set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] PROVENANCE`: the whole new line, with or without its number; the tool derives the kind. (as designed, the kind now derived)
79	- `merge N --into M FILE PROVENANCE`: removes N, rewrites M, rewrites every `F-N` pointer to `F-M`, one block each. (as designed)
80	- `remove N PROVENANCE`: refuses while a pointer to N remains, naming each. (as designed)
81	- `apply FILE PROVENANCE`: many changes from one file, checked against the resulting state, then written under one lock, or none. A new entry is written as `F-?1`, `F-?2` and so on, under its `## Section` heading, and the placeholder is replaced by the number everywhere in the file at apply, as the gather replaces `NEW-<rung>-<n>` for ledger rows (`climb-batch-workflow.md:160`). (as designed; the check against the resulting state and the placeholders are new)
82	- Provenance options: `--from PATH#HEADING` (repeatable; refused unless exactly one heading of the file holds it), `--commit HASH` (refused unless in `HEAD`'s history), `--by WHO`, `--note WHY`. A write with neither `--from` nor `--note` is refused. (as designed)
83	- Refused only for what breaks the store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve, no provenance, a line break. Never for size. (as designed)
84	- The lock file beside the record; the history appended first; the file replaced in one step. The tool does not commit. (as designed)
85	- The section parser reads `## ` and `### ` headings; an entry's section is the nearest heading above it of either level. (new)

88	
89	- `F-87`, `P-48`: the entry. (as designed)
90	- `F-87+`: the entry, the entries it points to and the entries that point to it, each once, one level. (as designed)
91	- `history:F-87`: the entry's blocks, oldest first. Nothing else: the linked entries are `F-87+`, and the report sections are a scout's `doc:` read. (changed: replaces `trace:`)
92	- A title query that matches no current title searches the former titles in the history and prints the entry with one line saying it was retitled. (as designed)
93	- `title_of` skips the number, in the numbering commit. (new)
94	- Not built: `history-find:`. The old texts are in git, and `grep` over `git show HASH:FILE` finds them. (changed)

96	**The checks.** `record.py check [--base COMMIT]`. The first four fail; the rest are reported.
97	
98	1. Every entry is one line of the form `- F-n **...**`; no number is on two lines.
99	2. Every number in a file has a `numbered` or `added` block, and every number in a history is in its file or its last block is `merged into` or `removed`.
100	3. Every `F-n` and `P-n` in either file resolves to a live entry.
101	4. With `--base`: every entry at COMMIT is its line now, or its line at COMMIT is the earlier line of a block in its history.
102	5. Reported: every `--from` path and every report section an entry cites resolves; the entries over 600 characters, with their sizes.
103	
104	(as designed for 1 to 5 and 7 to 8; the quoted-words rule of 4, the frozen-part hash of 6 and `--outside` of 9 are dropped: changed)
105

107	
108	- Each entry's number is its line at the base: FACTS lines 7 to 219, POSITIONS 7 to 145. The unused numbers stay unused. (as designed)
109	- The script rewrites both history files as above, with the former titles matched by exact title and by a shared opening of 60 characters. (changed: 3.6.3)
110	- It converts the pointers by title inside the record to numbers where one entry matches (about 83 inside FACTS, 67 from FACTS to POSITIONS, 21 the other way), and lists the ambiguous ones. 111	- It changes `fill.py` to resolve `{FACTS n}` by the number. (new)

120	
121	**Not built.** Ways 2 to 5; a stored index or typed links; anchors to report lines; a refusal by size; links beyond one level; a second tool for the coordinator (as designed). And: a frozen history, `trace:`, `history-find:`, `--outside`, the refresh of pointer words, the `title was` field, a YAML form, a `dry-run` flag (a writer applies in its own worktree and hands over the file). (changed)
122	
123	## 4. Tonight's run through it
124	
125	- The chunks are the sections, 20 to 32 entries each. FACTS: "The checker and the one library" in three (63 entries); "Landed semantics" (32); "Execution model" with "The harness and the gate" (41, in two if the writer's context asks); the arrays, the specification, the map and the ledger (32). "The container" waits for the `cloud-container` step, as the outline's 3.2.5 says. POSITIONS: "The goal", "History he knows", "The standard and the sources" and "The specification's revision" (23); "The one library and the compiled checker" (26); "Numbers" and "Arrays and the model program" with the three staying entries of "How we work" (26). 126	- The Sonnet scout of a chunk writes one file, at most 1,500 characters per entry: the number and title; for each report section the entry cites, whether `--check 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` resolves it, and its opening line; the commit that established the entry and the last that changed it (`git log --format='%h %ad %s' -S'<title words>' -- FACTS.md`); the status word of each ledger row named; the line of the latest earlier text under the same title in the old history (`git show HASH:FILE`) and its size; the entries that point to it (`F-n+`); for POSITIONS, his dated words on the entry from the old history's dated lines and the `CLIMB-BATCH-*` notes, each at most 300 characters with its date and time.
127	- The Opus writer of a chunk reads the entry definition, the chunk's entries and the scout's file. It writes the apply file: each entry's new line in the register, with its pointers by number, its merges and its removals; under each, its provenance line with `from` the sections that keep what it cut, `commit` the establishing commit, and a note saying why. It runs `apply` and `check --base` in its own worktree, reads the sizes, and hands the apply file to the coordinator with a short note: the points for the checker and each entry over 600 with the decision that needs it. The coordinator applies the file on `main`, runs `check --base`, commits the two files and pushes. Chunks apply one after another; the placeholders get their numbers there.
128	- The pilot: the checker's second chunk and POSITIONS's "The one library and the compiled checker", which hold the kit's FACTS 53, 55 and 58 and POSITIONS 48 and 60. The pass mark is the first run's totals (27 of 30 for either copy, `grades.md`, "3. Totals") with no scenario below the new entries' first-run score. The scenarios whose entries the pilot did not rewrite read the same text and are the control. A loss is repaired entry by entry, as his 10:14 rule says, and the pilot runs again on those entries before the rest.
129	- Tokens written, an estimate: nine scouts at about 0.15M, 1.4M; nine writers at about 0.35M, 3.2M; the coordinator's applies, checks and commits, 0.3M; the test, one reader and a grader, about 1.0M. 131	## 5. Decisions for the morning
132	
133	1. The history is rebuilt: the old texts leave the files, git keeps them at the commit the header names, and the sentence of "The record's form" (`POSITIONS.md:130`) that says the history holds every earlier text is rewritten to say it holds the provenance and the earlier lines from the numbering on. 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
3	the only way to write them.
4	
5	The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
6	each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
7	cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:
8	
9	  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |
10	
11	The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
12	explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
13	  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
14	               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
15	  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
16	               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
17	  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
18	               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
19	               specification does not say
20	  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
21	               path from the repository root, or `none`
22	  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
23	               notes 700
24	  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|
25	
26	Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
27	hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
28	way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
29	facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.
30

32	template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
33	changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
34	(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
35	became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

40	                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the

59	                             order

231	class Ledger:
232	    def __init__(self, path, text=None):
233	        self.path = path
234	        if text is None:
235	            with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
236	                text = f.read()
237	        self.lines = text.split('\n')
238	        self.sections, self.tables, self.rows = [], [], []
239	        section, table = None, None
240	        for i, ln in enumerate(self.lines):
241	            if ln.startswith('## '):
242	                section = Section(ln[3:].strip(), i)
243	                self.sections.append(section)
244	            if ln.startswith('|') and i + 1 < len(self.lines) and SEP.match(self.lines[i + 1]):
245	                table = Table(section, i, [ln, self.lines[i + 1]])
246	                self.tables.append(table)
247	                if section is not None:
248	                    section.tables.append(table)
249	            m = ROW.match(ln)
250	            if m:
251	                row = Row(int(m.group(1)), i + 1, section.title if section else None, table or TEMPLATE, ln)
252	                if table is None:
253	                    row.header = []     # a row above every table: read by the template, printed with no header
254	                self.rows.append(row)
255	                if table is not None:
256	                    table.rows.append(row)

268	        if len(hits) > 1:

277	    def section(self, title, exact=False):
278	        """The section with a row table whose title is TITLE, with or without its leading number; unless exact, else the one whose title holds it."""
279	        want = norm(title)
280	        secs = self.row_sections
281	        hits = [s for s in secs if norm(s.title) == want or norm(re.sub(r'^\d+\.\s*', '', s.title)) == want]
282	        if not hits and not exact:
283	            hits = [s for s in secs if want and want in norm(s.title)]
284	        if len(hits) == 1:
285	            return hits[0]
286	        if not hits:
287	            raise LedgerError('no section with a row table is titled "%s"; the sections: %s' % (
288	                title, '; '.join('"%s"' % s.title for s in secs)))
289	        raise LedgerError('"%s" names %d sections: %s' % (title, len(hits), '; '.join('"%s"' % s.title for s in hits)))

311	def norm(s):
312	    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
313	    for a, b in (('‘', "'"), ('’', "'"), ('“', ''), ('”', ''), ('`', ''), ('"', '')):
314	        s = s.replace(a, b)
315	    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip().casefold()

318	def word_pattern(w):
319	    if w.endswith('*') and len(w) > 1:
320	        return re.compile(r'(?<!\w)' + re.escape(w[:-1]))
321	    return re.compile(r'(?<!\w)' + re.escape(w) + r'(?!\w)')
322	
323	
324	def holds_all(words, text):
325	    t = norm(text)
326	    return all(word_pattern(w).search(t) for w in words)

329	def clip(text, n):
330	    """text cut to at most n characters at a word boundary, marked with … when cut."""
331	    if len(text) <= n:
332	        return text
333	    cut = text[:n + 1]
334	    return (cut[:cut.rfind(' ')] if ' ' in cut else text[:n]).rstrip() + ' …'
335

337	def first_sentence(text, n=HEAD_CLAIM):
338	    """The text up to its first full stop followed by a space, outside code spans, cut to n characters."""
339	    code = False
340	    for i, c in enumerate(text):
341	        if c == '`':
342	            code = not code
343	        elif not code and c == '.' and (i + 1 == len(text) or text[i + 1] == ' '):
344	            text = text[:i + 1]
345	            break
346	    return clip(text, n)

349	def escape_pipes(text):
350	    return re.sub(r'(?<!\\)\|', r'\\|', text)

353	def one_line(text):
354	    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()

357	def path_tokens(text):
358	    """(path, lines) for every token of text that names a file (a known extension) or a directory (a trailing slash)."""
359	    out = []
360	    for tok in re.split(r'[\s`,;()\[\]{}<>"\'*]+', text):
361	        tok = tok.rstrip('.:')
362	        path, _, lines = tok.partition(':')
363	        if lines and not re.match(r'\d', lines):
364	            continue
365	        if not path or not re.fullmatch(r'[\w.+/-]+', path) or not re.search(r'[A-Za-z]', path):
366	            continue
367	        base = path.rstrip('/').rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
368	        if path.endswith('/') and len(path) > 1:
369	            out.append((path, lines))
370	        elif PATH_EXT.search(path) and not PATH_EXT.fullmatch(base):
371	            out.append((path, lines))
372	    return out

375	def backtick_paths(line):
376	    """The paths a row cites in backticks, without their line numbers, each once, in order."""
377	    seen = []
378	    for span in re.findall(r'`([^`]+)`', line):
379	        for path, lines in path_tokens(span):
380	            if path not in seen:
381	                seen.append(path)
382	    return seen

385	def cites(line, file, at=None):
386	    """The citations of FILE in a row: (path, lines) for each, where a citation's path and FILE are equal or one ends with '/' and the other; at, a line, keeps those whose lines hold it."""
387	    hits = []
388	    for path, lines in path_tokens(line.replace('\\|', ' ')):
389	        if not (path == file or path.endswith('/' + file) or file.endswith('/' + path)):
390	            continue
391	        if at is not None and not any(lo <= at <= hi for lo, hi in line_ranges(lines)):
392	            continue
393	        hits.append((path, lines))
394	    return hits
395	
396	
397	def line_ranges(lines):
398	    out = []
399	    for part in re.findall(r'\d+(?:-\d+)?', lines or ''):
400	        lo, _, hi = part.partition('-')
401	        out.append((int(lo), int(hi or lo)))
402	    return out

413	class Linter:
414	    """Checks rows against the template; caches the test folders and the .tex headings it reads."""
415	    def __init__(self, root, numbers=()):
416	        self.root = root
417	        self.numbers = set(numbers)
418	        self._tests = None
419	        self._tex = {}
420	
421	    def tests(self):
422	        """Every file under the test folders, by its name and by its name without extension."""
423	        if self._tests is None:
424	            self._tests = collections.defaultdict(list)
425	            pf = os.path.join(self.root, 'ProjectFortress')
426	            folders = sorted(d for d in (os.listdir(pf) if os.path.isdir(pf) else [])
427	                             if (d == 'tests' or d.endswith('_tests') or d in TEST_FOLDERS_EXTRA)
428	                             and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(pf, d)))
429	            for d in folders:
430	                for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(os.path.join(pf, d)):
431	                    for name in files:
432	                        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, name), self.root)
433	                        self._tests[name].append(rel)
434	                        stem = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
435	                        if stem != name:
436	                            self._tests[stem].append(rel)
437	        return self._tests
438	
439	    def test_path(self, name):
440	        """The path from the root of the test NAME names (a path under a test folder, a file name, or a name without extension), else raise."""
441	        name = name.strip('`')
442	        if '/' in name:
443	            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, name)) and name in {p for ps in self.tests().values() for p in ps}:
444	                return name
445	            raise LedgerError('%s is not a file under the test folders (ProjectFortress/tests, *_tests, %s)' % (name, ', '.join(TEST_FOLDERS_EXTRA)))
446	        hits = self.tests().get(name, [])
447	        if len(hits) > 1:
448	            dotted = [p for p in hits if p.endswith('.test')]
449	            hits = dotted if len(dotted) == 1 else hits
450	        if len(hits) == 1:
451	            return hits[0]
452	        raise LedgerError('no test under the test folders is named %s' % name if not hits else
453	                          'the test name %s is ambiguous: %s' % (name, ', '.join(hits)))
454	
455	    def tex_headings(self, path):
456	        if path not in self._tex:
457	            heads = []
458	            with open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
459	                for ln in f:
460	                    m = TEX_HEAD.match(ln)
461	                    if m:
462	                        t = re.sub(r'\\[A-Za-z]+\*?', ' ', m.group(1))
463	                        heads.append(norm(t.replace('{', '').replace('}', '').replace('~', ' ')))
464	            self._tex[path] = heads
465	        return self._tex[path]

467	    def spec_file(self, path):
468	        for base in ('', 'Specification/'):
469	            full = os.path.join(self.root, base + path)
470	            if os.path.isfile(full):
471	                return full
472	        return None

474	    def lint_spec(self, cell):
475	        c = cell.strip()
476	        if c == 'silent':
477	            return []
478	        if not c:
479	            return [('spec', 'empty: write the .tex file and the section heading, or silent')]
480	        files = SPEC_FILE.findall(c.replace('`', ' '))
481	        if not files:
482	            return [('spec', 'cites no .tex file (write silent where the specification does not say): ' + clip(c, 70))]
483	        out, found = [], []
484	        for path, line in files:
485	            full = self.spec_file(path)
486	            if full:
487	                found.append(full)
488	            else:
489	                out.append(('spec-path', '%s is not a file from the repository root or Specification/' % path))
490	            if line and not path.startswith(FROZEN):
491	                out.append(('spec-line', 'a line number only against %s: %s%s' % (FROZEN, path, line.strip())))
492	        heads = [a or b for a, b in QUOTED.findall(c)]
493	        if not heads:
494	            out.append(('spec-section', 'no section heading in quotes after the file'))
495	        elif found:
496	            known = [h for f in found for h in self.tex_headings(f)]
497	            for h in heads:
498	                if not any(norm(h) in k for k in known):
499	                    out.append(('spec-section', '"%s" is no heading of %s' % (clip(h, 60), ', '.join(os.path.relpath(f, self.root) for f in found))))
500	        return out
501	
502	    def lint_reproducer(self, cell):
503	        c = cell.strip()
504	        if c == 'none':
505	            return []
506	        if not c:
507	            return [('reproducer', 'empty: write the test, a probe path from the repository root, or none')]
508	        tok = c[1:-1] if c.startswith('`') and c.endswith('`') and c.count('`') == 2 else c
509	        if not tok or re.search(r'[\s`]', tok):
510	            return [('reproducer', 'not one path or test name: ' + clip(c, 70))]
511	        path = re.sub(r':\d[\d,-]*$', '', tok)
512	        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.root, path)) or ('/' not in path and path in self.tests()):
513	            return []
514	        return [('reproducer-path', '%s is no path from the repository root and no test name' % clip(path, 80))]
515	
516	    def lint(self, row):
517	        """[(rule, detail)] for one row."""
518	        out = []
519	        if not row.line.rstrip().endswith('|'):
520	            out.append(('cells', 'the line does not end with |'))
521	        if row.split == 'lenient':
522	            out.append(('pipe', 'a bare | inside a cell splits it (%d cells at every pipe); write \\|' % len(split_cells(row.line))))
523	        elif len(row.cells) != len(HEADER):
524	            out.append(('cells', '%d cells; the template has %d' % (len(row.cells), len(HEADER))))
525	        if row.num is None or not (row.cells and row.cells[0].isdigit()):
526	            out.append(('number', 'the # cell is not a number: %s' % clip(row.cells[0] if row.cells else '', 20)))
527	        status = row.status
528	        if status not in STATUSES:
529	            out.append(('status', 'not one word of the seven: %s' % clip(status, 70)))
530	        k = row.klass
531	        if k == DASH:
532	            if status not in NO_CLASS:

567	                    out.append((r, 'order', 'row %d after row %d in its table' % (r.num, prev.num)))
568	                prev = r
569	        by = collections.defaultdict(list)

577	            if missing:
578	                out.append((None, 'number', 'numbers missing from 1-%d: %s' % (max(by), ', '.join(map(str, missing)))))

620	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), prefix='.ledger-', suffix='.tmp')

2	"""Print a rung's briefing, or any slice of the project's record, in bounded parts.
3	
4	Called by facts-extract.sh beside it; run that with --help for the usage.
5	The record: explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md (what is established, grouped
6	by area, each entry cited by its title), explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md
7	(one line per standalone note), POSITIONS.md and POSITIONS-history.md beside
8	them (Pavol's decisions, each under its bold title, and their dated history),
9	the gap ledger explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md (one table row per gap),
10	the maps under explorations/coordinator/map/, any other note by path and
11	heading, such as a judge's ruling or a section of the specification's .tex
12	sources, and code by the declaration it starts at.

35	# script reads them whole since 2026-09-27: printed first to every agent they
36	# cost more than they saved (explorations/reviews/worker-context-cost.md), and a

58

68	                         title is its bold opening, or where it has none, its

88	                         heading holds HEADING, down to the next heading of its level
89	  doc:PATH#HEADING       the same for any note, PATH from the repository root, such
90	                         as a judge's ruling; doc:PATH alone prints the whole note;
91	                         in a .tex or .tick file the headings are its \\chapter, \\section,
92	                         \\subsection, \\subsubsection and \\paragraph titles,
93	                         matched with their macros dropped; a heading equal to
94	                         HEADING wins over the headings that merely hold it, and
95	                         HEADING may be a path, A > B, for B's section inside A's
96	  map:FILE#HEADING@WORDS, doc:PATH#HEADING@WORDS
97	                         only the table rows and list items of that section that
98	                         hold every one of WORDS, a row under its table's header,
99	                         and the paragraphs whose bold lead holds them
100	  code:PATH#FROM         the declaration that starts on the one line of PATH that
101	                         holds FROM, with its line numbers: in .java, .scala and
102	                         .js through the brace that closes it, elsewhere (.fss,
103	                         .fsi) through its more indented lines and its end
104	  code:PATH#FROM..TO     from the declaration at FROM through the end of the
105	                         one at the first line after it that holds TO
106	WORDS match as whole words, or as the start of one when a word ends in *.
107	Matching ignores case, backticks and double quotes, reads curly quotes as
108	straight ones, and takes any run of spaces as one space.
109	
110	  --check             print one line per query, what it matches, where, and its
111	                      size in bytes, then the size of the whole output, and
112	                      nothing else; exit 1 unless every query matches exactly
113	                      one place (an index or ledger-find topic: at least one line)
114	  --part N            print part N of the output (default 1)
115	  --page-bytes N      the size of a part (default 28000)
116	  --root DIR          read the record and every map: and doc: path from the
117	                      checkout at DIR instead of this tool's own
118	  --common            first print the record's shared sections: the map's
119	                      README "Terms used here", "The shape of the system" and

121	                      explorations/repo-internals.md whole; no role of the batch
122	                      script reads them whole, and a planner reads them to

128	def norm(s):
129	    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
130	    for a, b in (('‘', "'"), ('’', "'"), ('“', ''), ('”', ''), ('`', ''), ('"', '')):
131	        s = s.replace(a, b)
132	    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip().casefold()

135	def word_pattern(w):
136	    """A word matches a whole word; with a trailing * it matches the start of
137	    one (wrap* finds wrap, wraps and wrapping)."""
138	    if w.endswith('*') and len(w) > 1:
139	        return re.compile(r'(?<!\w)' + re.escape(w[:-1]))
140	    return re.compile(r'(?<!\w)' + re.escape(w) + r'(?!\w)')

143	def holds_all(words, text):
144	    t = norm(text)
145	    return all(word_pattern(w).search(t) for w in words)

187	def title_of(text):
188	    body = text[2:]
189	    if body.startswith('**'):
190	        end = body.find('**', 2)
191	        if end > 2:
192	            return body[2:end]
193	    # No bold title: the opening words, up to the first colon, semicolon or
194	    # full stop followed by a space, outside code spans.
195	    code = False
196	    for i, c in enumerate(body):
197	        if c == '`':
198	            code = not code
199	        elif not code and c in ':;.' and body[i + 1:i + 2] == ' ':
200	            return body[:i]
201	    return body[:200]

205	    """A POSITIONS.md entry's head: its first line up to the first colon
206	    followed by a space, outside code spans, which is where his words begin;
207	    a colon right after the opening date does not end it."""
208	    body = text.split('\n', 1)[0][2:]

211	    for i, c in enumerate(body):

213	            code = not code
214	        elif not code and c == ':' and body[i + 1:i + 2] == ' ' and not (lead and i < lead.end()):

275	def md_sections(lines):
276	    """(level, heading, first line, last line) for every heading, 1-based and
277	    inclusive; a section runs to the line before the next heading of its level
278	    or a higher one. Headings inside fenced code are not headings."""
279	    heads, fence = [], False
280	    for n, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
281	        if ln.startswith('```') or ln.startswith('~~~'):
282	            fence = not fence
283	            continue
284	        m = None if fence else re.match(r'(#{1,6}) +(.*\S)', ln)
285	        if m:
286	            heads.append([len(m.group(1)), m.group(2), n, None])
287	    last = len(lines)
288	    while last > 0 and not lines[last - 1].strip():
289	        last -= 1
290	    for i, h in enumerate(heads):
291	        end = last
292	        for later in heads[i + 1:]:
293	            if later[0] <= h[0]:
294	                end = later[2] - 1
295	                break
296	        while end > h[2] and not lines[end - 1].strip():
297	            end -= 1
298	        h[3] = end
299	    return [tuple(h) for h in heads]

304	TEX_HEAD = re.compile(r'\s*\\(part|chapter|section|subsection|subsubsection|paragraph)\*?\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\s*\{(.*)\}')

307	def tex_title(t):
308	    """A .tex heading's text with its macros and braces dropped: the words a key
309	    can name, since a key holds no backslash."""
310	    t = re.sub(r'\\[A-Za-z]+\*?', ' ', t)
311	    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', t.replace('{', '').replace('}', '').replace('~', ' ')).strip()

314	def tex_sections(lines):
315	    """(level, title, first line, last line) for every sectioning command of a
316	    .tex file, as md_sections does for markdown; a commented-out one is not one."""
317	    heads = []
318	    for n, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
319	        m = TEX_HEAD.match(ln)
320	        if m:
321	            heads.append([TEX_LEVELS[m.group(1)], tex_title(m.group(2)), n, None])
322	    last = len(lines)
323	    while last > 0 and not lines[last - 1].strip():
324	        last -= 1
325	    for i, h in enumerate(heads):
326	        end = last
327	        for later in heads[i + 1:]:
328	            if later[0] <= h[0]:
329	                end = later[2] - 1
330	                break
331	        while end > h[2] and not lines[end - 1].strip():
332	            end -= 1
333	        h[3] = end
334	    return [tuple(h) for h in heads]

337	def resolve_doc(rec, spec):
338	    """'map:FILE#HEADING[@WORDS]' or 'doc:PATH#HEADING[@WORDS]' -> (path, heading or None, words or None)."""
339	    kind, rest = spec.split(':', 1)
340	    path, _, heading = rest.partition('#')
341	    heading, _, words = heading.partition('@')
342	    path = path.strip()
343	    if kind == 'map':
344	        path = MAPS + path
345	    if not path.endswith('.md') and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(rec.root, path)):
346	        path += '.md'
347	    return os.path.join(rec.root, path), (heading.strip() or None), (norm(words).split() or None)

353	def select_rows(lines, a, b, words):
354	    """The table rows, list items and bold-lead paragraphs of lines a..b that
355	    hold every one of words, as (first, last, header lines); a list item keeps
356	    its indented continuation, and a paragraph that opens with a bold lead, as
357	    a batch record's do, runs to the next such paragraph or heading and is
358	    matched by its lead alone."""
359	    out, header, n = [], [], a
360	    while n <= b:
361	        ln = lines[n - 1]
362	        if ln.startswith('**'):
363	            end = n
364	            while end < b and not lines[end].startswith('**') and not lines[end].startswith('#'):
365	                end += 1
366	            while end > n and not lines[end - 1].strip():
367	                end -= 1
368	            close = ln.find('**', 2)
369	            if holds_all(words, ln[2:close] if close > 2 else ln):
370	                out.append((n, end, []))
371	            n = end + 1
372	            continue
373	        if ln.startswith('|'):
374	            if n < b and re.match(r'\|\s*:?-{3,}', lines[n]):
375	                header = [ln, lines[n]]
376	                n += 2
377	                continue
378	            if holds_all(words, ln):
379	                out.append((n, n, header))
380	            n += 1
381	            continue
382	        m = ITEM.match(ln)
383	        if m:
384	            end, indent = n, len(m.group(1))
385	            while end < b and lines[end].strip() and not lines[end].startswith('|') \
386	                    and (len(lines[end]) - len(lines[end].lstrip())) > indent:
387	                end += 1
388	            if holds_all(words, '\n'.join(lines[n - 1:end])):
389	                out.append((n, end, []))
390	            n = end + 1
391	            continue
392	        n += 1
393	    return out

401	def decl_end(lines, n, braces):
402	    """The last line of the declaration that starts on line n (1-based)."""
403	    if braces:
404	        depth, opened = 0, False
405	        for k in range(n, min(len(lines), n + 800) + 1):
406	            ln = re.sub(r'"(\\.|[^"\\])*"|' + r"'(\\.|[^'\\])*'", '""', lines[k - 1])
407	            ln = ln.split('//', 1)[0]
408	            for c in ln:
409	                if c == '{':
410	                    depth, opened = depth + 1, True
411	                elif c == '}':
412	                    depth -= 1
413	            if opened and depth <= 0:
414	                return k
415	        return n
416	    indent = len(lines[n - 1]) - len(lines[n - 1].lstrip())
417	    end, k = n, n + 1
418	    while k <= len(lines):
419	        ln = lines[k - 1]
420	        if ln.strip():
421	            ind = len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())
422	            if ind > indent:
423	                end = k
424	            else:
425	                if ind == indent and re.match(r'end\b', ln.strip()):
426	                    end = k
427	                break
428	        k += 1
429	    return end

432	def find_code(rec, spec):
433	    f = Found(spec)
434	    rest = spec[len('code:'):]
435	    path, _, anchors = rest.partition('#')
436	    frm, _, to = anchors.partition('..')
437	    path = os.path.join(rec.root, path.strip())
438	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
439	        f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no such file: ' + rec.rel(path)
440	        return f
441	    if not frm.strip():
442	        f.bad, f.missing = True, 'a code: key names the line its declaration starts at, after #'
443	        return f
444	    lines = read_lines(path)
445	    want = norm(frm)
446	    starts = [n for n, ln in enumerate(lines, 1) if want in norm(ln)]
447	    if not starts:
448	        f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no line of %s holds "%s"' % (rec.rel(path), frm.strip())
449	        return f
450	    f.bad = len(starts) > 1
451	    braces = path.endswith(BRACES)
452	    spans = []
453	    for a in starts:
454	        b = decl_end(lines, a, braces)
455	        if to.strip():
456	            want_to = norm(to)
457	            later = [n for n in range(a + 1, len(lines) + 1) if want_to in norm(lines[n - 1])]
458	            if not later:
459	                f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no line of %s after :%d holds "%s"' % (rec.rel(path), a, to.strip())
460	                return f
461	            b = max(b, decl_end(lines, later[0], braces))
462	        spans.append((a, b))
463	    for a, b in spans:
464	        width = len(str(b))
465	        f.blocks.append(('== %s:%d-%d' % (rec.rel(path), a, b),
466	                         '\n'.join('%*d  %s' % (width, n, lines[n - 1]) for n in range(a, b + 1))))
467	    f.where = ', '.join('%s:%d-%d' % (rec.rel(path), a, b) for a, b in spans) + ('' if len(spans) == 1 else '  (%d lines hold it, not one)' % len(spans))
468	    return f

473	class Found:
474	    """What one query found: where, its blocks, and whether --check refuses it."""
475	    def __init__(self, query, label=None):
476	        self.query = query
477	        self.label = label or query
478	        self.where = ''
479	        self.blocks = []          # (context line, text)
480	        self.bad = False
481	        self.missing = None       # why nothing was found

484	def find_doc(rec, spec, one):
485	    f = Found(spec)
486	    path, heading, words = resolve_doc(rec, spec)
487	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
488	        f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no such file: ' + rec.rel(path)
489	        return f
490	    lines = read_lines(path)
491	    if heading is None:
492	        last = len(lines)
493	        while last > 0 and not lines[last - 1].strip():
494	            last -= 1
495	        hits = [(1, last, '(the whole note)')]
496	    else:
497	        heads = tex_sections(lines) if path.endswith(TEX) else md_sections(lines)
498	        # HEADING may name a path, "A > B": B's section inside A's.
499	        hits = None
500	        for part in heading.split(' > '):
501	            q = norm(part)
502	            within = [(a, b, h) for (lvl, h, a, b) in heads if q in norm(h)
503	                      and (hits is None or any(pa <= a and b <= pb and (pa, pb) != (a, b) for pa, pb, ph in hits))]
504	            # A heading that is the query exactly wins over the ones that hold it.
505	            hits = [x for x in within if norm(x[2]) == q] or within
506	        # A heading inside another matched section is printed with it.
507	        hits = [x for x in hits if not any(y is not x and y[0] <= x[0] and x[1] <= y[1] for y in hits)]
508	    if not hits:
509	        f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no heading holds it'
510	        return f
511	    if words:
512	        rows = []
513	        for a, b, h in hits:
514	            rows += [(r, e, hd, a, b) for (r, e, hd) in select_rows(lines, a, b, words)]
515	        if not rows:
516	            f.bad, f.missing = True, 'no table row or list item of %s holds every word' % ', '.join(
517	                '%s:%d-%d' % (rec.rel(path), a, b) for a, b, h in hits)
518	            return f
519	        f.bad = len(rows) > 1
520	        for r, e, hd, a, b in rows:
521	            ctx = '== %s:%d-%d, %s' % (rec.rel(path), a, b, 'the row at :%d' % r if r == e else 'the item at :%d-%d' % (r, e))
522	            f.blocks.append((ctx, '\n'.join(hd + lines[r - 1:e])))
523	        f.where = ', '.join('%s:%d%s' % (rec.rel(path), r, '' if r == e else '-%d' % e) for r, e, hd, a, b in rows) \
524	            + ('' if len(rows) == 1 else '  (%d rows, not one)' % len(rows))
525	        return f
526	    f.bad = len(hits) > 1 and one
527	    for a, b, h in hits:
528	        ctx = '== %s:%d-%d' % (rec.rel(path), a, b)
529	        # A long section is split at blank lines into pieces of about a
530	        # quarter of a part, so that parts fill evenly; each piece keeps the
531	        # section's reference.
532	        piece = []
533	        for n in range(a, b + 1):
534	            piece.append(lines[n - 1])
535	            if n < b and not lines[n].strip() and nbytes('\n'.join(piece)) > PAGE_BYTES // 4:
536	                f.blocks.append((ctx, '\n'.join(piece).strip('\n')))
537	                piece = []
538	        if piece:
539	            f.blocks.append((ctx, '\n'.join(piece).strip('\n')))
540	    f.where = ', '.join('%s:%d-%d' % (rec.rel(path), a, b) for a, b, h in hits) + ('' if len(hits) == 1 else '  (%d sections)' % len(hits))
541	    return f

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print a rung's briefing, or any slice of the record (FACTS.md, INDEX.md, POSITIONS.md, the ledger, the maps, a note by heading); --help for the usage.
exec python3 "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/facts-extract.py" "$@"
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check a consolidation of FACTS.md or POSITIONS.md: every entry of the file as
it stood at BASE appears verbatim, as a whole entry, in the file now or in its history file,
and in exactly one of the two.

An entry is a top-level bullet ("- ") with its indented continuation lines.
Written 2026-09-27 for the POSITIONS split (886a06e1d, repaired in cda7d86a6,
whose first pass had lost 20 entries' text); generalised 2026-09-29 to either file.

usage: check-verbatim.py BASE FILE HISTORY
  e.g. check-verbatim.py 8c1158937 explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md explorations/coordinator/FACTS-history.md
Exit 0 when no entry is missing and none is in both files; 1 otherwise.
"""
import subprocess, sys

if len(sys.argv) != 4:
    sys.exit(__doc__)
base, path, hpath = sys.argv[1:]
old = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'{base}:{path}'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
new = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
hist = open(hpath, encoding='utf-8').read()

def entries(text):
    out, cur, start = [], None, 0
    for i, ln in enumerate(text.split('\n'), 1):
        if ln.startswith('- '):
            if cur is not None:
                out.append((start, cur))
            cur, start = ln, i
        elif cur is not None and ln.startswith('  '):
            cur += '\n' + ln
        else:
            if cur is not None:
                out.append((start, cur))
            cur = None
    if cur is not None:
        out.append((start, cur))
    return out

# Whole entries are compared, not substrings: an entry cut to a prefix of an
# older text of itself would otherwise count as in the history too (2026-10-13).
E = entries(old)
N = {e for _, e in entries(new)}
H = {e for _, e in entries(hist)}
in_new = [n for n, e in E if e in N]
in_hist = [n for n, e in E if e in H]
both = [n for n, e in E if e in N and e in H]
missing = [(n, e) for n, e in E if e not in N and e not in H]
print(f'entries in {path} at {base}: {len(E)} ({len(old.encode())} bytes); now {len(new.encode())} bytes')
print(f'  verbatim in the file now:        {len(in_new)}')
print(f'  verbatim in the history file:    {len(in_hist)}')
print(f'  in both (should be 0):           {len(both)} {both}')
print(f'  in neither (should be 0):        {len(missing)}')
for n, e in missing:
    print(f'    MISSING old line {n}: {e[:100]}')
print('moved to history (old line numbers):', ' '.join(str(n) for n in in_hist))
sys.exit(1 if missing or both else 0)
